headline: Majors hold above 200-day lines with neutral momentum, but whales moving size onto exchanges while spot ETF demand wavers.
paragraphs: The regime is intact: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all trade above their 200-day simple moving averages, and four of the five show golden crosses (XRP is the exception). This is the setup of a market in recovery, not one in collapse. But the momentum picture is flat. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 49.0 and Ethereum at 50.7, both centered, neither accelerating. More important, MACD is below signal across all majors, meaning the recent uptrend has lost its punch. The month tells a different story: Bitcoin up 18.4% over the last 30 days, Ethereum up 28.6%, Solana up 31.8%. That rally has hit a wall on the week. Bitcoin down 5.6% over the last seven sessions, Ethereum down 4.4%, Solana down 8.8%, XRP down 9.5%, Doge down 11.7%, ADA down 12.6%. The regime is not broken, but the recent momentum has clearly stalled, and the weekly deterioration is sharper than the daily pin bars suggest.

Positioning tells a different story. Funding is broadly positive and accelerating upward: Bitcoin at 6.5% annualized (0.0059% over eight hours), Ethereum at 1.1% (0.001%), XRP at 1.9% (0.0017%). This means long traders are paying lenders to hold their bets. Solana is the outlier, trading at negative funding of negative 6.4% annualized (negative 0.0058% over eight hours), indicating shorts are expensive and crowded. Open interest is heavy across the board: Bitcoin at $2.12 billion, Ethereum at $1.49 billion, Solana at $250 million. Long-to-short ratios are tilted bullish: Bitcoin 1.78, Ethereum 2.12, Solana 2.39, XRP 2.95, Doge 4.65. That last number for Doge (which sits negative 71.6% from its 12-month high) is striking. When positioning is this skewed, liquidations can be violent. Over the last three to six hours, shorts have been liquidated sharply in Ethereum ($1.08 million versus $150k in longs), Solana ($2.48 million versus $191k in longs), and Doge ($3.1k versus $413k in longs). The tape is asymmetric: long liquidations are happening in coins with extreme retail tilt, shorts are being wrung out of the larger caps.

Flows reveal a tension. Over the last 24 hours, $76.87 million in Bitcoin moved onto Binance, while $28.66 million in Cronos moved off Crypto.com. The weekly picture widens the frame: $1.199 billion moved onto exchanges in the week ending August 26, then $49 million in the week of September 2, then $406 million in the week of September 9, and $558 million in the week ending September 16. The direction is consistent onto exchanges, and the dollar value is material. This is supply pressure. At the same time, Bitcoin spot ETF saw an outflow of $288.7 million on September 15, and the five-session net is negative $544.9 million. Ethereum ETF is split: outflow of $56.7 million on the day, but inflow of $285.6 million over the last five sessions. Traditional finance is not consistently bidding. Stablecoins stand at $310.28 billion, up 1.34% over the last month, a modest float. The combination reads as a market where whales are deploying liquidity onto centralized exchanges while traditional spot vehicles are facing net redemptions.

Sentiment is neutral at 51 (range of 41 to 74 over the last 30 days), sitting in the middle of its recent band. Fear and Greed is not signaling capitulation or euphoria, just equilibrium. The daily action contradicts this in a quiet way: prices up fractionally on the day across all majors (Bitcoin up 0.3%, Ethereum up 0.2%, Doge up 0.2%), yet the macro momentum down hard on the week. The crowd is calm while the tape shows distributional pressure. Realized volatility is high in the smaller caps (XRP at 98.7%, Doge at 79.7%), moderate in the mid-caps (SOL 70.4%, ETH 73.8%), and lower in the largest (BTC 49.0%, BNB 46.6%). Altcoins are moving harder than Bitcoin, and some are fractional: Arbitrum up 13.14% on the day, Injective down 12.8%, Raydium down 11.19%. That dispersion within a flat regime is noise, not signal.

Bitcoin dominance is 58.5%, total market cap at $2.598 trillion and down 5.64% on the day. The retreat is broad, not concentrated. To watch: whether Bitcoin reclaims its resistance or rolls over on the week, whether MACD crosses back above signal (a momentum reset), whether the whale inflows onto exchanges reverse direction (a sign that big holders are taking risk off the table), and whether funding stays positive or flips negative (an early warning that longs are unwinding). The regime survives as long as the majors hold their 200-day lines; a break below would be a condition worth naming. For now, the tape shows a market in suspension, neither capitulating nor rallying, with size moving into centralized exchanges and spot ETF demand fragmented.
